video_title: Explaining Steph Curry, Ayesha Curry's Charity Impact In Oakland

quotes.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
quotes.summary_phrase: Growth and impact of the Eat. Learn. Play. charity event
quotes.excerpt: the generosity that Workday has brought to this event and that's allowed it to grow

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: Starting with you, Chris, when I say the number seven, how exciting does that feel to get to, we're closing on a decade doing this, of course with Aneel as well too?

text_blocks.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
text_blocks.text: Time flies. It is pretty surreal that we're at seven years and to see the way that this event has grown. It's pretty remarkable. The generosity that Workday has brought to this event and that's allowed it to grow into something that's raised well over $10 million now that's 100% of that goes right back out into the community. It's remarkable, it's gratifying, and it's also the most fun day of the year.

quotes.speaker: Aneel Bhusri
quotes.summary_phrase: Aneel Bhusri on the Currys' community impact in Oakland
quotes.excerpt: It all starts with this guy and the Currys. We're just the enabler.

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: Aneel, do you allow yourself to look back at the beginning of this and see how much it's grown to these stages?

text_blocks.speaker: Aneel Bhusri
text_blocks.text: I haven't recently until I drove up here today and I thought, my god, the seventh year. It all starts with this guy and the Currys. We're just the enabler. We bring together a bunch of people that are willing to invest in what Steph and Ayesha and Chris want to do in Oakland and the Bay Area for kids and it's pretty amazing what they've done.

quotes.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
quotes.summary_phrase: Eat. Learn. Play. impact on Oakland school playground renovations
quotes.excerpt: over 10,000 kids every day are going and playing, learning and growing on these state of the art spaces

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: Just 10 days ago was the 25th school year that Eat. Learn. Play. has transformed in Oakland. When I say 25, what does that number mean to you?

text_blocks.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
text_blocks.text: It means that there's a lot of kids who are finally getting the spaces that they deserve. When we started remodeling schoolyards across the entire district, there's 49 elementary schools, really the play spaces were just blacktop and an old playground and a couple basketball hoops. But now, through this work, over 10,000 kids every day are going and playing, learning and growing on these state of the art spaces. That ambition was really driven by Workday and Aneel. When we did our second, it was Aneel who called me the next day and said that was amazing, can we do all of them? And that's been the journey that we've been on over the last couple of years.

quotes.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen and Ayesha Curry's ambition to disrupt the status quo
quotes.excerpt: how can we disrupt things in a really positive way all in the interest of making sure kids in Oakland have the happy, healthy, joyful childhoods that they deserve.

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: Chris, you keep using the word ambition. I love to hear that word, especially for an event like this for both of you. How have you seen the Currys show their ambition throughout the Bay Area and Oakland specifically?

text_blocks.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
text_blocks.text: You see the way that Stephen, you see Stephen on the basketball court and you see some of the stuff that he tries that no one else will or has. I like to think we have a little bit of that at Eat. Learn. Play. where we see a situation that might need some fixing and we're just ambitious enough to go, you know what, that doesn't have to be the status quo. How can we disrupt things in a really positive way all in the interest of making sure kids in Oakland have the happy, healthy, joyful childhoods that they deserve.

quotes.speaker: Aneel Bhusri
quotes.summary_phrase: Aneel Bhusri on the character of Stephen and Ayesha Curry
quotes.excerpt: I've known Steph for a long time. He's one of the greatest basketball players of all time. He's an even better human being and the same applies to Ayesha

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: Aneel, how have you seen the Currys show their ambition throughout the Bay Area and Oakland specifically?

text_blocks.speaker: Aneel Bhusri
text_blocks.text: Stephen and Ayesha, they just always show up. They just show up and that goes so far and so long in the community. I've known Steph for a long time. He's one of the greatest basketball players of all time. He's an even better human being and the same applies to Ayesha and that's what's so magical about it.

quotes.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award win
quotes.excerpt: Stephen winning the Muhammad Ali Humanitarian Award, all for the work that he and Ayesha do in Oakland

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: I think about the award that he won this year when it comes to the Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award. That was an award that it felt like he wanted to share part of with both of you, and with all of Oakland, with the entire Bay Area. How awesome was that to see him on that stage winning an award that was bigger than basketball?

text_blocks.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
text_blocks.text: That was a special moment, Stephen winning the Muhammad Ali Humanitarian Award, all for the work that he and Ayesha do in Oakland. To be there with Aneel and get to watch it, it was great and the Currys are the best. It was really nice to see them be recognized and honored for the work that they do literally day in and day out to help Oakland kids.
